case_name: State of Jammu and Kashmir v Sudershan Chakkar and Another
respondent:

Delay condoned.
Special leave granted.

facts: On a First Information Report lodged by the Director, Food & Supplies, Jammu, a case under sections 120-B, 467 and 409 IPC and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act was registered against the two respondents herein, who at the material time were the Tehsil Supply Officers of Ramban, one Nijamuddin, a Store Keeper, and two transport contractors, the allegation being that all of them hatched a criminal conspiracy and pursuant thereto misappropriated foodgrains and empty bags of the Food and Supplies Department worth Rs. 3,22,119.36 after forging official documents.
The Police Vigilance Organisation took up investigation of the case and submitted a charge-sheet, whereupon the Special Judge, Anti Corruption, Jammu took cognizance.

Thereafter he heard the parties on the question of framing of charges and held that a prima facie case was made out only against the other three arraigned but not against the two respondents. Accordingly he discharged them by his order dated June 28, 1993,
issues: Whether the learned Courts below erred in basing their respective orders on the findings
Whether the Court is required to confine its attention to documents referred to under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure only
petitioner_arguments: The question whether the respondents omitted to do their mandatory duties for months together designedly or negligently can be inferred only on an over all view of all the materials collected during investigation and not in isolation

In a case instituted upon a Police Report the Court is required, at the time of framing of the charges, to confine its attention to documents referreded to under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure only
court_reasoning: The learned Courts below erred in basing their respective orders on the above findings

That apart in a case instituted upon a Police Report the Court is required, at the time of framing of the charges, to confine its attention to documents referred to under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure only
holding: Allow this appeal set aside the impugned orders and direct the learned Trial Judge to proceed with the matter afresh in accordance with law and in the light of the observations made hereinbefore

By way of abundant caution we make it clear that in dealing with the matter the learned Judge shall not allow himself to be influenced by anything said in this order in regard to the merits of the case
